baseline.name: Insertion sort
baseline.approach: Insert each next element into its sorted prefix by shifting larger predecessors.
baseline.time: O(n^2) worst case; O(n) for already sorted input

archived.name: Iterative in-place heapsort
archived.time: O(n log n) worst case; O(n) heap build

why: Heap extraction limits each repositioning to a root-to-leaf path rather than moving a whole prefix.
quantitative_comparison: Reverse-order insertion sort can shift n(n-1)/2 elements. The archive does n-1 heap extractions, each with O(log n) sift-down work. No elapsed speed multiplier is derived from these bounds.
tradeoffs: Insertion sort can win for small or nearly sorted input and is stable; heapsort is unstable and returns the mutated input pointer. No claim of superiority over every O(n log n) sort is made.
evidence_basis: Static worst-case operation-growth comparison against a named sort baseline; no benchmark.
